Reuters reported that Russia's antitrust watchdog has opened a formal investigation into Apple for failing to pre-install the state-backed instant messaging app MAX and the Russian app store RuStore on its devices. Details below.

Russia files antitrust lawsuit against Apple

Since Russia passed a law in 2019 requiring device makers to offer domestic apps on products sold locally, Apple and Russian authorities have been engaged in a protracted tug-of-war.

When the law came into effect in 2021, Apple reached an arrangement whereby Russian users setting up a new iPhone would see a list of Russia-developed recommended apps, rather than having them automatically pre-installed.

In March 2022, after Russia's invasion of Ukraine, Apple stopped selling and exporting products in the country, and removed the RT and Sputnik news apps from the App Store outside Russia. That September, Apple cited UK sanctions as the reason for removing several apps belonging to Russian tech company VK.

Last year, Russia began requiring that the state-backed instant messaging app MAX be pre-installed on all new smartphones and tablets sold in the country, while extending the mandate to install the RuStore app store to Apple devices. Apple has not complied with either requirement.

Tensions escalated further in June, when Apple removed MAX from the Russian App Store, followed later that month by the removal of several VK-developed apps. Apple said the takedowns were carried out to comply with sanctions.

This prompted Russia's Federal Antimonopoly Service (FAS) to issue an order requiring the company to remedy what it described as discrimination against domestic software by 15 July. Apple reportedly partially complied, allowing the Russian search engine to be pre-installed with iOS 26.6, but did not implement the provisions relating to MAX and RuStore.

According to Reuters, since Apple failed to fully comply with the warning, Russia has now opened a formal antitrust case against the company.

From the report:

It remains unclear what penalties Apple could face if Russia finds it has violated its competition laws. In 2024, Russia calculated a fine of approximately 200 decillion dollars (a 2 followed by 33 zeros) against Google for its years-long refusal to restore blocked Russian state and pro-Kremlin channels on YouTube.

Apple has yet to respond to the investigation.
